items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: They had Scott Joplin's book and a teacher of the tunes.

ctx.x: He was straight in jazz and everything, but they played most of Scott Joplin's music. They had Scott Joplin's book and a teacher of the tunes. That's why they named the office after one of Scott Joplin's great tunes of Maple Leaf. He was currently popular over the time of Mario Perez.
What album did your grandfather play out of? Is it all ballgreens? What do you play?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: All them people was playing Scott Joplin's legitimate thing.

ctx.x: Yeah. You're lucky if you understand it. But Jelly had a thing, you know.
He'd go like this. [DEMONSTRATES] And he's gone, in another key.

Well, Jelly Roll, you know, played stomp. He slowed down rag, and he called it stomps -- stomp-down. You see, everybody, Eubie Blake, everybody...Joe Jordan... All them people was playing Scott Joplin's legitimate thing. Jelly Roll took it and slowed it down. [SINGS A REFRAIN] It's probably because if you're old and you're a hustler... [SINGS, SNAPS FINGERS] See, that's a stomp-down. [SINGS REFRAIN] And you can see they're gonna like Jelly Roll's music, because if you play... [SINGS FAST TEMPO]... you're all out…
